newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Uninvited mourner urges corpse to wake up.
newsitem.headline: Uninvited mourner urges corpse to wake up.

text.p: Grief and drink unhinged burly ex-U.S. marine Willis Baynes-Nash who tried to wake up a corpse, a court was told on Wednesday.

Shocked mourners watched as he entered a funeral home uninvited and struck the body of Mattie Twomey, which was lying in its open coffin for the final farewells of friends and relatives, Macroom court heard.
"I thought I was in a dream. I went up and saw the corpse and I hit it and said 'wake up, wake up" Baynes-Nash said in court.
Baynes-Nash said he had been drinking gin to console himself on the death of a friend from cancer and news of a heart attack which had stricken his aunt.
The mourners escorted him from the funeral home where Twomey was lying but Baynes-Nash then assaulted the son of the owner of the establishment.
He then went to a nearby supermarket in this southern Irish town and threatened to kill wheelchair-bound Tess Lucey before vaulting a wall and fleeing.
He was pursued by Lucey's son, Jimmy, and husband, Christy, and wrestled to the ground until an off-duty policeman arrived on the scene.
The judge said the case was so serious he needed time to think about a penalty and adjourned the case until June 18.
